subject: Clarifying failover accountability for private deployment - Eden Health
messages:
From: Marcela Ruiz <marcela.ruiz@edenhealth.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@edenhealth.com
Date: Sun, 6 Sep 2026 08:32:00 -0700
Subject: Clarifying failover accountability for private deployment - Eden Health

Hi Michael,

Thanks again for running through the post-mortem yesterday. The incident timeline you sent was helpful, but our Compliance and Ops teams are asking for a clearer statement of where Redwood draws the line for remediation responsibility for private deployments (specifically the customer-controlled edge components).

Two concrete asks from our side:
1) Can you confirm which components Redwood accepts SLA liability for in our Private deployment (control plane, core inference mesh, KV-store availability, etc.) versus what remains our responsibility (edge peering, customer NAT, on-prem load balancers)?
2) For faults originating in customer-controlled infra, what's the escalation and evidence workflow Redwood will accept to apply an SLA exception? We need this documented for our auditors.

I've attached our preliminary incident timeline (incident_timeline_q3.csv) to help narrow the windows.

Appreciate a short call if that helps — our lead on this is in Ops (ops@edenhealth.com).

Best,
Marcela
Marcela Ruiz
Head of Platform Operations
Eden Health

From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>
To: Marcela Ruiz <marcela.ruiz@edenhealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 6 Sep 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarifying failover accountability for private deployment - Eden Health

Hi Marcela —

Thanks for the clear asks and for the timeline. I've pulled together a short runbook and a proposed SLA amendment that map responsibilities to the stack. I'm sending the draft runbook and an internal checklist; please treat them as a starting point for the auditor documentation. Attach: redwood_private_runbook_draft_v1.docx

Quick summary here so it's easy to reference:
- Redwood responsibility (Default): control plane, model serving mesh within customer VPC that runs on Redwood-managed instances, persistent storage backing model artifacts and service discovery. We accept standard availability calculations for those components.
- Customer responsibility (Default): any customer-managed border devices (on-prem load balancers, NATs, transit VPNs, colocation cross connects), DNS records under customer control, and any third-party appliances in the path.

For incidents originating in customer-controlled infra, our evidence workflow to consider an SLA exception is:
1) Customer provides network/edge telemetry correlating to the incident window (pcap snippets, NAT logs, ASN-level reachability checks).
2) Customer runbook showing attempted failover steps and timestamps (we need to know whether retries/route failovers were executed).
3) If telemetry isn't available, we accept signed vendor support tickets (carrier or colo) and an affidavit from customer network lead for the window.
Once we have the evidence, our SREs will run a root-cause correlation within the SLA window (we target 5 business days for the initial determination). If the event is attributed to customer infra, we apply the carveout and annotate uptime metrics accordingly.
If you agree, we can draft an appendix to the SLA that lists the acceptable artifact types and the response timelines. I've cc'd Kimberly (Legal interface) and Naomi (SRE lead) to loop them into the drafting and to scope the telemetry requirements.
Would you be available for a quick 30-minute sync on Monday to align on the appendix language?
Best,
Mike Grant
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Clarifying failover accountability for private deployment - Eden Health

Mike,

Thanks — this is already helpful. A couple of clarifying points from our side:
- For "Redwood-managed instances" inside our VPC, do you mean instances you spin up (via Redwood Dedicated/Private install) or machine images that we run in our environment? Historically we've had vendors define that differently.
- Our auditors will want a maximum evidence window (e.g., how far back you will accept telemetry) and the minimum fidelity (flow logs vs. full packet capture).

We can do Monday 10:00am PT for the 30-minute sync. Ops will bring our network lead and procurement.

Marcela

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Marcela Ruiz <marcela.ruiz@edenhealth.com>, Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 7 Sep 2026 09:24:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarifying failover accountability for private deployment - Eden Health

Marcela, Mike —

Thanks for the back-and-forth. For the SLA appendix, Legal proposes the following practical compromise (high level):

- Attribution buckets: (A) Redwood-controlled stack, (B) Customer-controlled edge, (C) Third-party transit/carrier.
- For (B) events, Redwood will accept the following artifacts within a 30-day evidence window: flow logs (preferred), carrier incident IDs, and runbook timestamped screenshots. Full packet capture will be "nice to have" but not required.
- For (B) events where evidence demonstrates attempted failover per the customer's runbook, Redwood will treat the event as a carveout and will not count the period against the Redwood availability calculation.
- If evidence is inconclusive, Redwood will open a joint forensic review with a target of 10 business days to reach a determination.
- We will add a short mutual-attestation clause for on-call handoff (names, rotation, escalation numbers) to be appended to the contract.

Action items:
1) Mike / Naomi to propose the specific evidence artifact list and example log snippets we accept (I'll insert the legal language after we see that).
2) Marcela to confirm Eden's retention windows for flow logs and whether they can produce carrier tickets.
3) We'll prepare a one-page appendix and circulate for signature via DocuSign.

Attaching a redline of the proposed SLA language for internal review. Attach: proposed-sla-amendment.pdf
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Commercial
Redwood Inference
